articleBody:
Removing an old bathtub is more than simple demolition—it involves plumbing lines, subfloor condition, and disposal logistics. Before hiring a remodeling contractor, review this practical checklist.

What to Prepare Before You Start

- [ ] Tub material identification — Knowing whether your tub is fiberglass, steel, acrylic, or heavy cast iron determines the tools, crew size, and labor required.
- [ ] Working water shutoff valves — Confirming functional shutoffs prevents emergency shutoff disruptions to the rest of the house during disconnection.
- [ ] Dedicated plumbing access location — Identifying an access panel or adjacent wall opening allows your contractor to disconnect drain lines without damaging finished walls.
- [ ] Surrounding tile and drywall plan — Deciding how many inches of wall finish to open up ensures a clean transition for future shower panels or tile.
- [ ] Drain size evaluation — Checking the current waste pipe confirms whether plumbing needs expansion to match a walk-in shower drain.
- [ ] Subfloor moisture inspection — Planning for subfloor checks ensures rot or soft spots get repaired before installing any replacement fixture.
- [ ] Written haul-away and disposal terms — Confirming debris removal in the estimate avoids surprise dumpster fees or heavy scrap left on your property.
- [ ] Required local trade permits — Verifying permit responsibilities ensures any drain relocation or plumbing alterations meet local residential codes.

How to use this checklist:
Walk through each item with your contractor during your initial consultation to keep your tub removal organized, safe, and on schedule. For hands-on help in Aurora and the greater Denver area, call Abraham Becerra at HH Remodeling LLC at 303-505-0866.
